docs.title: ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph
docs.text:
"Where Knowledge Connects, Agents Reason, and Intelligence Emerges."

An enterprise-ready Hybrid Document Intelligence Platform built with Google Agent Development Kit (ADK). Authenticate with Neon PostgreSQL, ingest documents through a live 5-step dual vector + graph pipeline, explore interactive Neo4j knowledge topologies, and converse with a multi-tool reasoning agent.

docs.title: Why Hybrid Vector + Knowledge Graph RAG?
docs.text:
Traditional RAG systems rely solely on vector similarity over isolated chunks, often missing global entity relationships or exact technical identifiers. ADK Agentic RAG unites three complementary paradigms under a single Google ADK agent:

Hybrid Search (Neon PostgreSQL) Knowledge Graph (Neo4j) Google ADK Multi-Tool Agent

Combines 768-dimensional semantic vector search (pgvector HNSW cosine similarity, 70% weight) with PostgreSQL Full-Text Search (ts_rank_cd GIN index, 30% weight) in a single SQL query—capturing both conceptual meaning and exact keyword/identifier matches.

SELECT chunk_id, filename, content,
       (1 - (embedding <=> %(query_vec)s::vector)) AS vector_similarity,
       ts_rank_cd(to_tsvector('english', content), plainto_tsquery('english', %(query)s)) AS keyword_score,
       (0.7 * (1 - (embedding <=> %(query_vec)s::vector)) +
        0.3 * ts_rank_cd(to_tsvector('english', content), plainto_tsquery('english', %(query)s))) AS combined_score
FROM document_chunks
WHERE user_id = %(user_id)s
ORDER BY combined_score DESC
LIMIT 5;

Uses Gemini 2.5 Flash Structured Outputs during ingestion to extract typed domain entities (Technology, Model, Organization, Person, Concept, Metric) and directed [:RELATES_TO] facts into Neo4j, enabling multi-hop relationship traversal.

MATCH (s:Entity {user_id: $user_id})-[r:RELATES_TO {user_id: $user_id}]->(t:Entity {user_id: $user_id})
WHERE toLower(s.name) CONTAINS $term OR toLower(r.fact) CONTAINS $term
RETURN s.name AS source, r.relation_type AS relation_type, t.name AS target, r.fact AS fact
LIMIT 15;

The LlmAgent powered by Gemini 2.5 Pro autonomously chooses which tool—or combination of tools—to invoke for each user question, returning inline citations for both document chunks ([Source: file.pdf, chunk 2]) and graph facts ([Graph: EntityA -> USES -> EntityB]).

root_agent = LlmAgent(
    name="hybrid_rag_kg_agent",
    model=AGENT_MODEL,
    description="Hybrid Vector + Knowledge Graph Agentic RAG assistant.",
    instruction=build_agent_instruction,
    tools=[
        hybrid_search,
        vector_search,
        graph_search,
        get_entity_relationships,
    ],
)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The FastAPI backend (app/api.py) exposes REST endpoints on http://localhost:8000 (interactive Swagger UI available at http://localhost:8000/docs).

All protected endpoints require an Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token> header obtained from /auth/login or /auth/signup.

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Returns server liveness status.

curl http://localhost:8000/health

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph API"
}

docs.title: POST /auth/signup
docs.text:
Creates a new user account in the Neon PostgreSQL users table and returns a signed HS256 JWT Bearer token.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/signup \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Alice Morgan",
    "email": "alice@company.com",
    "password": "securepassword123"
  }'

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "success",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "user": {
    "user_id": "user_9f8e7d6c5b4a3210",
    "email": "alice@company.com",
    "name": "Alice Morgan",
    "created_at": "2026-11-06T18:30:00+00:00"
  }
}

docs.title: POST /auth/login
docs.text:
Authenticates an existing user by email and password against Neon PostgreSQL.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "alice@company.com",
    "password": "securepassword123"
  }'

Response (200 OK): Same structure as /auth/signup.

docs.title: GET /auth/me
docs.text:
Verifies the Bearer JWT token and returns the active user profile.

curl http://localhost:8000/auth/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: GET /ingest/status
docs.text:
Returns database connectivity and aggregate counts across Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector) and Neo4j for the authenticated user.

curl http://localhost:8000/ingest/status \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "ready",
  "vector_db": "Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector + FTS)",
  "vector_db_connected": true,
  "graph_db": "Neo4j Knowledge Graph",
  "graph_db_connected": true,
  "embedding_model": "gemini-embedding-001",
  "agent_model": "gemini-2.5-pro",
  "graph_extraction_model": "gemini-2.5-flash",
  "total_documents": 2,
  "total_chunks_in_db": 28,
  "total_entities_in_graph": 34,
  "total_relationships_in_graph": 41,
  "supported_file_types": [".csv", ".docx", ".htm", ".html", ".json", ".log", ".md", ".pdf", ".pptx", ".txt", ".xls", ".xlsx", ".xml"]
}

docs.title: GET /ingest/progress
docs.text:
Returns real-time step-by-step execution status (pending, running, completed, error) for each of the 5 ingestion stages for the authenticated user.

curl http://localhost:8000/ingest/progress \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: POST /documents/upload
docs.text:
Uploads a file and runs the 5-step dual ingestion pipeline into Neon PostgreSQL and Neo4j.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/documents/upload \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -F "file=@/path/to/document.pdf"

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "success",
  "filename": "document.pdf",
  "document_id": "52e1a9d0-8c1a-4f3b-9b12-0192837465ab",
  "chunks_created": 14,
  "text_length": 15240,
  "entities_extracted": 18,
  "relationships_extracted": 22
}

docs.title: GET /documents
docs.text:
Lists all ingested documents belonging to the authenticated user.

curl http://localhost:8000/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: DELETE /documents/{document_id}
docs.text:
Cascade-deletes a document and all of its chunks from Neon PostgreSQL and removes its relationships, document node, and orphaned entities from Neo4j.

curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/documents/52e1a9d0-8c1a-4f3b-9b12-0192837465ab \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: GET /graph
docs.text:
Returns the user's Neo4j knowledge graph (nodes, edges, and stats) for visualization in the Knowledge Graph tab.

curl "http://localhost:8000/graph?limit=150" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: GET /graph/entity/{entity_name}
docs.text:
Returns the 1-hop incoming and outgoing relationships for a specific entity in Neo4j.

curl "http://localhost:8000/graph/entity/PostgreSQL?depth=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: POST /chat
docs.text:
Sends a question to the Google ADK LlmAgent equipped with hybrid_search, vector_search, graph_search, and get_entity_relationships.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "question": "How are entities extracted and connected across my documents?",
    "session_id": "session_demo_1"
  }'

Response (200 OK): 

{
  "status": "success",
  "question": "How are entities extracted and connected across my documents?",
  "answer": "Entities are extracted using Gemini Structured Outputs and stored in Neo4j...",
  "tools_used": ["hybrid_search", "graph_search"],
  "session_id": "session_demo_1",
  "user_id": "user_9f8e7d6c5b4a3210"
}

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: The ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform is engineered as a modular, multi-tenant Hybrid Document Intelligence system combining Google Agent Development Kit (google-adk), Gemini 2.5, Neon Console Serverless PostgreSQL (pgvector + Full-Text Search), and Neo4j.

docs.title: Architectural Pillars
docs.text:
• Neon PostgreSQL Authentication

    Stateless HS256 JWT Bearer authentication backed by a users table in Neon PostgreSQL with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (260,000 iterations) password hashing.

  • 5-Step Dual Ingestion Engine

    Asynchronous worker pipeline that parses 12 document formats, chunks text semantically, embeds in batches (768-dim), indexes in Neon Postgres, and extracts entities into Neo4j.

  • Google ADK Multi-Tool Agent

    LlmAgent (gemini-2.5-pro) equipped with 4 specialized retrieval tools (hybrid_search, vector_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships) and dynamic user context injection.

  • Interactive Bioluminescent UI

    React 18 + Vite single-page workspace featuring real-time per-step ingestion telemetry, tool execution badges, dual citations, and an interactive SVG Neo4j topology explorer.

docs.title: 2. Backend Module Architecture (app/)
docs.text: Module File Responsibility Configuration app/config.py Loads .env, validates GOOGLE_API_KEY, configures DATABASE_URL, NEO4J_*, JWT_*, AGENT_MODEL, and GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL. Database Layer app/database.py Manages the Neon PostgreSQL ThreadedConnectionPool (with TCP keepalives, connection health checks, and URL normalization) and the Neo4j driver (GraphDatabase.driver). Automatically initializes pgvector, tables, HNSW/GIN indexes, and Neo4j constraints on startup. Authentication app/auth.py Implements PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing (260,000 iterations), HS256 JWT signing/verification, user registration/login against the Neon users table, and the get_current_user FastAPI security dependency. Format Parsers app/parsers.py Dispatches uploaded files by extension (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .xls, .pptx, .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .xml, .html, .log) to specialized text extractors. Semantic Chunker app/chunking.py Splits extracted document text along markdown headers, paragraphs, and sentences (chunk_size=1200, overlap=200) to preserve semantic coherence. Embeddings app/embeddings.py Wraps google-genai gemini-embedding-001 (768 dimensions) with batching (50 chunks per call) for high-throughput document ingestion and single-query embedding. Vector & Hybrid Store app/rag_store.py Executes Neon PostgreSQL CRUD (add_document_chunks, delete_document_chunks, list_user_documents) and retrieval (search_documents pure vector cosine search and hybrid_search_documents combining 70% vector similarity + 30% ts_rank_cd full-text score). Knowledge Graph Store app/graph_store.py Extracts structured ExtractedEntity and ExtractedRelationship objects from chunks using gemini-2.5-flash and persists/queries them in Neo4j via parameterized Cypher queries. Dual Ingestion Pipeline app/ingest.py Orchestrates the 5-step ingestion pipeline and maintains real-time per-user step telemetry (_user_ingestion_progress) polled by the frontend UI. Google ADK Agent app/agent.py Defines root_agent (LlmAgent) equipped with 4 tools (hybrid_search, vector_search, graph_search, get_entity_relationships) and dynamic system instructions injecting the active user_id. REST API app/api.py Exposes FastAPI endpoints for Auth, Upload, Live Ingestion Progress, Documents, Knowledge Graph, and Agentic Chat. Runs heavy ingestion in asyncio.to_thread using OS temp storage (/tmp/adk_rag_uploads) so Uvicorn --reload is never interrupted.

docs.title: 3. End-to-End Sequence Flows
docs.text:
1. Authentication Flow 2. 5-Step Dual Ingestion Flow 3. Multi-Tool Agentic Retrieval Flow 4. Cascade Deletion Flow 
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as React Frontend
    participant API as FastAPI (/auth/*)
    participant Auth as app/auth.py
    participant Neon as Neon PostgreSQL (users)

    User->>UI: Enter Email & Password (Sign In or Sign Up)
    UI->>API: POST /auth/signup or POST /auth/login
    API->>Auth: register_user() / authenticate_user()
    Auth->>Neon: SELECT / INSERT user record
    Neon-->>Auth: User row (user_id, email, name, password_hash)
    Auth->>Auth: Verify PBKDF2-SHA256 hash & sign HS256 JWT
    Auth-->>API: {token, user}
    API-->>UI: 200 OK {token, user}
    UI->>UI: Save JWT in localStorage & attach Authorization: Bearer <token>
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as React UI (UploadTab / IngestionTab)
    participant API as FastAPI (app/api.py)
    participant Ingest as app/ingest.py
    participant Gemini as Google Gemini API
    participant Neon as Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector)
    participant Neo4j as Neo4j Knowledge Graph

    User->>UI: Select file & click "Ingest into Neon Postgres & Neo4j"
    UI->>UI: Switch to Ingestion Pipeline tab & poll /ingest/progress
    UI->>API: POST /documents/upload (multipart file + Bearer JWT)
    API->>Ingest: asyncio.to_thread(ingest_document)

    Note over Ingest: Step 1 — Text Extraction
    Ingest->>Ingest: parse_file(file_path) -> raw text

    Note over Ingest: Step 2 — Semantic Chunking
    Ingest->>Ingest: chunk_text(text, size=1200, overlap=200)

    Note over Ingest: Step 3 — Batched Embeddings
    Ingest->>Gemini: get_embeddings_batch(chunks) [gemini-embedding-001]
    Gemini-->>Ingest: 768-dim float vectors

    Note over Ingest: Step 4 — Neon PostgreSQL Indexing
    Ingest->>Neon: INSERT documents + execute_values(document_chunks)

    Note over Ingest: Step 5 — Neo4j Graph Extraction
    Ingest->>Gemini: extract_graph_from_chunks() [gemini-2.5-flash JSON]
    Gemini-->>Ingest: Entities & Relationships
    Ingest->>Neo4j: Cypher MERGE (:Entity), (:Document), [:RELATES_TO]
    Ingest->>Neon: UPDATE documents SET entities_count, relationships_count

    Ingest-->>API: Summary dict (chunks, entities, relationships)
    API-->>UI: 200 OK Ingestion Complete
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as React ChatTab
    participant API as FastAPI (POST /chat)
    participant Runner as Google ADK Runner (LlmAgent)
    participant Rag as app/rag_store.py (Neon Postgres)
    participant Graph as app/graph_store.py (Neo4j)

    User->>UI: Ask question
    UI->>API: POST /chat {question, session_id} + Bearer JWT
    API->>Runner: runner.run_async(user_id, session_id, message)

    alt Hybrid / Vector Query
        Runner->>Rag: hybrid_search(query, user_id) or vector_search(query, user_id)
        Rag-->>Runner: Top-K ranked document chunks + similarity scores
    end

    alt Entity / Relationship Query
        Runner->>Graph: graph_search(query, user_id) or get_entity_relationships(entity_name, user_id)
        Graph-->>Runner: Matched Neo4j entities & (Source)-[RELATES_TO]->(Target) facts
    end

    Runner-->>API: Final synthesized response + tool call events
    API-->>UI: {answer, tools_used, session_id}
    UI-->>User: Render Markdown answer with Tool Badges & [Source]/[Graph] citations
flowchart LR
    A["DELETE /documents/{document_id}"] --> B["Neon PostgreSQL:\nDelete from documents & document_chunks\nWHERE document_id = :id AND user_id = :uid"]
    B --> C["Neo4j Step 1:\nDelete RELATES_TO edges\nWHERE r.document_id = :id AND r.user_id = :uid"]
    C --> D["Neo4j Step 2:\nDETACH DELETE (:Document {id: uid::doc_id})"]
    D --> E["Neo4j Step 3:\nPrune orphaned (:Entity) nodes\nwith no remaining MENTIONED_IN or RELATES_TO links"]

docs.title: 4. Multi-Tenant Security & Data Isolation
docs.text:
Defense-in-Depth Tenant Partitioning

Every data record across the entire stack is partitioned by the authenticated user_id extracted from the verified HS256 JWT token:

  1. Authentication Layer (app/auth.py): Extracts and verifies the user_id (sub claim) on every protected API request.
  2. Neon PostgreSQL (app/rag_store.py): Every SELECT and DELETE query enforces WHERE user_id = %s.
  3. Neo4j Knowledge Graph (app/graph_store.py): Every node ID is prefixed with <user_id>:: (e.g., user_123::postgresql) and every Cypher MATCH filters on {user_id: $user_id}.
  4. Google ADK Session Context (app/agent.py): ADK chat sessions are keyed by (app_name, user_id, session_id) and build_agent_instruction(ReadonlyContext) injects the active user_id directly into the agent's system prompt.

docs.title: Agentic Chat & Graph Tools
docs.text: The chat subsystem uses Google Agent Development Kit (google-adk) and Gemini (gemini-2.5-pro) to reason across both Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector + Full-Text Search) and the Neo4j Knowledge Graph.

docs.title: Multi-Tool Agent Architecture (app/agent.py)
docs.text:
The root agent (root_agent) is an instance of google.adk.agents.LlmAgent configured with four specialized tools:

flowchart TD
    Question["User Question in Agentic Chat"] --> Agent["Google ADK LlmAgent\n(gemini-2.5-pro)"]
    Agent -->|Exact terms + semantics| T1["1. hybrid_search\n(70% pgvector cosine + 30% PostgreSQL FTS)"]
    Agent -->|Broad conceptual similarity| T2["2. vector_search\n(100% pgvector cosine similarity)"]
    Agent -->|Entities & factual triplets| T3["3. graph_search\n(Neo4j Entity & RELATES_TO keyword match)"]
    Agent -->|1-hop / 2-hop graph neighborhood| T4["4. get_entity_relationships\n(Neo4j Cypher neighborhood traversal)"]
    T1 --> Synthesis["Synthesized Markdown Response\nwith Tool Badges + [Source] & [Graph] Citations"]
    T2 --> Synthesis
    T3 --> Synthesis
    T4 --> Synthesis

docs.title: 1. hybrid_search(query, user_id, top_k=5)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/rag_store.py -> hybrid_search_documents()
  • How It Works: Embeds query with gemini-embedding-001 (768-dim) and runs a single SQL query on Neon PostgreSQL combining cosine similarity (0.7 weight) and English full-text rank ts_rank_cd (0.3 weight).
  • Best For: Technical questions, specific names, numbers, dates, and general factual questions over uploaded documents.

docs.title: 2. vector_search(query, user_id, top_k=5)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/rag_store.py -> search_documents()
  • How It Works: Queries document_chunks ordered purely by pgvector cosine distance (embedding <=> query_vec).
  • Best For: Conceptual, thematic, or paraphrased queries where exact keywords may not appear in the source text.

docs.title: 3. graph_search(query, user_id, limit=15)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/graph_store.py -> search_knowledge_graph()
  • How It Works: Tokenizes the query and searches Neo4j (:Entity) names, categories, descriptions, and [:RELATES_TO] facts scoped to user_id.
  • Best For: Discovering how people, organizations, technologies, models, and concepts connect across one or more documents.

docs.title: 4. get_entity_relationships(entity_name, user_id, depth=1)
docs.text:
• Backend Function: app/graph_store.py -> get_entity_relationships_from_graph()
  • How It Works: Finds the matching (:Entity) node in Neo4j and traverses all incoming and outgoing [:RELATES_TO] edges plus [:MENTIONED_IN] document links.
  • Best For: Deep-diving into a specific entity's direct connections and dependencies.

docs.title: Dynamic User Context Injection
docs.text:
To guarantee that the agent always queries only the signed-in user's data without asking the user for their ID, build_agent_instruction(readonly_context: ReadonlyContext) dynamically injects the authenticated user_id into the system prompt on every turn:

def build_agent_instruction(readonly_context: ReadonlyContext) -> str:
    user_id = "default_user"
    if readonly_context and getattr(readonly_context, "session", None):
        user_id = getattr(readonly_context.session, "user_id", None) or "default_user"
    return (
        f"... The current authenticated user's `user_id` is EXACTLY: \"{user_id}\". "
        f"Whenever you call ANY tool, you MUST pass `user_id=\"{user_id}\"` ..."
    )

docs.title: Tool Execution Tracking & Dual Citations
docs.text:
In app/api.py, the /chat endpoint inspects the ADK event stream (event.get_function_calls()) during runner.run_async(...) and collects the ordered list of invoked tool names into tools_used:

{
  "status": "success",
  "question": "How does the platform store vectors and knowledge graph facts?",
  "answer": "The platform stores 768-dimensional embeddings in Neon PostgreSQL [Source: architecture.md, chunk 0] and extracts entities into Neo4j [Graph: FastAPI Backend -> USES -> Neo4j].",
  "tools_used": ["hybrid_search", "graph_search"],
  "session_id": "session_a8b9c0",
  "user_id": "user_9f8e7d6c5b4a3210"
}

The frontend ChatMessage.jsx component renders: - Tool Execution Badges at the top of the assistant message bubble (hybrid_search, graph_search) - Source Chunk Citations: [Source: filename, chunk N] - Knowledge Graph Citations: [Graph: EntityA -> RELATION -> EntityB]

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to deploy the ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform to production using cloud services: - Vector & Auth Database: Neon Console Serverless PostgreSQL - Knowledge Graph Database: Neo4j AuraDB - FastAPI Backend: Render (configured via render.yaml) - React Frontend: Netlify (configured via frontend/netlify.toml)

docs.title: 1.1 Neon Console PostgreSQL (pgvector)
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Neon Console and create a project.
  2. Copy your pooled connection string (postgresql://user:pass@ep-...pooler...neon.tech/dbname?sslmode=require).
  3. On first startup, the backend automatically executes CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; and creates the users, documents, and document_chunks tables (or run sql/schema.sql directly in the Neon SQL Editor).

docs.title: 1.2 Neo4j AuraDB
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Neo4j Aura Console and create a Free or Professional instance.
  2. Copy your connection URI (neo4j+s://xxxxxxxx.databases.neo4j.io), username (neo4j), and generated password.

docs.title: 2. Deploy the Backend to Render
docs.text:
1. Push your repository to GitHub.
  2. Sign in to Render and create a new Web Service connected to your repository.
  3. Configure the service (or use the included render.yaml Blueprint):
  4. Runtime: Python 3
  5. Build Command: pip install -r requirements.txt
  6. Start Command: uvicorn app.api:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
  7. Set the following Environment Variables in Render:
  8. GOOGLE_API_KEY: Your Gemini API key
  9. DATABASE_URL: Your Neon Console PostgreSQL connection string (including ?sslmode=require)
  10. JWT_SECRET_KEY: A strong random secret key for signing JWT tokens
  11. JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS: 168
  12. NEO4J_URI: Your Neo4j AuraDB URI (neo4j+s://...)
  13. NEO4J_USERNAME: neo4j
  14. NEO4J_PASSWORD: Your Neo4j password
  15. NEO4J_DATABASE: neo4j
  16. AGENT_MODEL: gemini-2.5-pro
  17. GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL: gemini-2.5-flash
  18. TOP_K: 5
  19. Deploy and copy your live Render URL (e.g., https://adk-rag-backend.onrender.com).

docs.title: 3. Deploy the Frontend to Netlify
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Netlify and click Add new site → Import an existing project.
  2. Select your GitHub repository and configure:
  3. Base directory: frontend
  4. Build command: npm run build
  5. Publish directory: frontend/dist
  6. Under Environment Variables, add:
  7. VITE_API_URL: Your Render backend URL (without a trailing slash)
  8. Click Deploy site.

Also displays Neon PostgreSQL & Neo4j metrics and the dual storage architecture diagram. docs.title: API Client (frontend/src/api.js)
docs.text: All HTTP calls are centralized in frontend/src/api.js: - Automatically attaches Authorization: Bearer <jwt_token> from localStorage. - Automatically clears expired sessions on HTTP 401 and dispatches an adk_auth_expired window event so App.jsx smoothly returns the user to the Sign In page.

docs.title: Ingestion Pipeline
docs.text: The 5-step dual ingestion pipeline converts raw uploaded files into both searchable 768-dimensional vector chunks in Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector) and structured entities and relationships in the Neo4j Knowledge Graph, while streaming real-time step progress to the UI.

docs.title: 5-Step Dual Ingestion Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Upload["Uploaded File
(app/api.py -> /tmp/adk_rag_uploads)"] --> Step1["Step 1: Format-Specific Text Extraction
(app/parsers.py)"]
    Step1 --> Step2["Step 2: Structure-Aware Semantic Chunking
(app/chunking.py — 1200 chars, 200 overlap)"]
    Step2 --> Step3["Step 3: Batched Gemini Embeddings
(app/embeddings.py — gemini-embedding-001, 768-dim)"]
    Step3 --> Step4["Step 4: Neon PostgreSQL Indexing
(app/rag_store.py — pgvector HNSW + FTS GIN)"]
    Step4 --> Step5["Step 5: Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction
(app/graph_store.py — gemini-2.5-flash Structured JSON -> Cypher MERGE)"]

docs.title: Step 1: Format-Specific Text Extraction (app/parsers.py)
docs.text:
parse_file(file_path) inspects the lowercase file extension and routes the file to the appropriate parser:

Extension Library Extraction Details .pdf pymupdf (import pymupdf as fitz) Opens each page in sequence and extracts text blocks via page.get_text("text"). .docx python-docx Extracts all non-empty paragraphs followed by all table rows formatted as cell1 \| cell2. .xlsx openpyxl Loads workbook with data_only=True (evaluated formula values) and formats each sheet under [Sheet: Name]. .xls xlrd Iterates legacy Excel sheets and formats non-empty rows. .pptx python-pptx Extracts text frames and tables slide-by-slide under [Slide N]. .txt, .md, .log Built-in open() Reads UTF-8 text directly. .csv csv Joins each CSV row with ,. .json json Parses JSON and pretty-prints with indent=2. .xml, .html, .htm xml.etree.ElementTree / regex Strips tags and normalizes whitespace into clean text.

docs.title: Step 2: Structure-Aware Semantic Chunking (app/chunking.py)
docs.text:
Instead of slicing text at arbitrary character offsets (which breaks sentences and tables mid-thought), chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1200, overlap=200) preserves document structure:

  1. Line Normalization: Converts to and collapses 3+ consecutive newlines into .
  2. Paragraph & Header Segmentation: Splits along paragraph breaks ( ) and Markdown headings (#, ##, ###).
  3. Greedy Paragraph Packing: Accumulates complete paragraphs into the current chunk as long as total length remains \(\le 1200\) characters.
  4. Sentence-Boundary Fallback: If a single paragraph exceeds 1200 characters, splits along sentence boundaries ((?<=[.!?])\s+).
  5. Contextual Overlap: Carries the trailing 200 characters of chunk \(i\) into the start of chunk \(i+1\) so concepts spanning chunk boundaries remain intact.

docs.title: Step 3: Batched Gemini Embedding Generation (app/embeddings.py)
docs.text:
get_embeddings_batch(texts, batch_size=50) generates 768-dimensional vectors for all chunks using gemini-embedding-001:

response = client.models.embed_content(
    model="gemini-embedding-001",
    contents=batch,
    config=types.EmbedContentConfig(output_dimensionality=768),
)

Batching up to 50 chunks per API request significantly reduces ingestion latency compared to sequential per-chunk calls.

docs.title: Step 4: Neon PostgreSQL Vector + Full-Text Indexing (app/rag_store.py)
docs.text:
add_document_chunks(...) inserts the document metadata into documents and bulk-inserts all chunks into document_chunks using psycopg2.extras.execute_values:

  • Vector Index (pgvector HNSW): Indexes embedding vector_cosine_ops for fast cosine similarity search.
  • Full-Text Index (PostgreSQL GIN): Indexes to_tsvector('english', content) for keyword and phrase matching.

docs.title: Step 5: Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction (app/graph_store.py)
docs.text:
add_document_to_graph(...) extracts domain entities and factual relationships from the chunks and merges them into Neo4j:

  1. Structured LLM Extraction:
  2. Sends batches of 4 chunks to gemini-2.5-flash configured with response_mime_type="application/json" and response_schema=ChunkGraphExtraction.
  3. Extracts canonical ExtractedEntity nodes (name, category, description) and ExtractedRelationship edges (source, target, relation_type, fact).
  4. Neo4j Cypher Persistence:
  5. Creates/merges the (:Document {id: user_id::document_id}) node.
  6. Merges each (:Entity {id: user_id::lower(name)}) node and links (e)-[:MENTIONED_IN]->(d).
  7. Merges directed (source:Entity)-[:RELATES_TO {relation_type, document_id, user_id}]->(target:Entity) edges storing the supporting fact.
  8. Metadata Sync:
  9. Updates documents.entities_count and documents.relationships_count in Neon PostgreSQL so the Documents tab displays accurate counts for every file.

docs.title: Live Per-User Progress Tracking (app/ingest.py)
docs.text:
During ingestion, ingest_document() updates an in-memory per-user state dictionary (_user_ingestion_progress[user_id]) before and after each of the 5 steps.

The frontend polls GET /ingest/progress every 800ms while an upload is active, receiving:

{
  "active": true,
  "filename": "architecture_overview.pdf",
  "current_step": 3,
  "error": null,
  "steps": {
    "1": { "status": "completed", "detail": "Extracted 14,820 characters" },
    "2": { "status": "completed", "detail": "Created 15 semantic chunks" },
    "3": { "status": "running", "detail": "Generating 768-dim vectors for 15 chunks..." },
    "4": { "status": "pending", "detail": "Waiting" },
    "5": { "status": "pending", "detail": "Waiting" }
  }
}

docs.title: Installation & Local Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up the ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform locally.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Version Purpose Python 3.10+ (3.12 recommended) FastAPI backend & Google ADK agent Node.js & npm 18+ React 18 + Vite frontend Google Gemini API Key Free / Paid Tier Google AI Studio Neon Console PostgreSQL Free / Serverless Tier Neon Console (pgvector enabled automatically) Neo4j Database AuraDB Free or Local 5.x Neo4j Aura Console or local Docker instance

docs.title: Step 1: Create & Activate Virtual Environment
docs.text:
cd /path/to/adk_rag
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Step 2: Install Python Dependencies
docs.text: pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Environment Variables (.env)
docs.text:
Copy .env.example to .env:

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env with your credentials:

GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key_here
AGENT_MODEL=gemini-2.5-pro
GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash

# Neon Console PostgreSQL Connection String
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://neondb_owner:password@ep-xxx-pooler.us-east-1.aws.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require

# JWT Secret for Neon Authentication
JWT_SECRET_KEY=replace-with-a-long-random-secret-string
JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS=168

# Neo4j AuraDB or Local Neo4j Instance
NEO4J_URI=neo4j+s://xxxxxxxx.databases.neo4j.io
NEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j
NEO4J_PASSWORD=your_neo4j_password_here
NEO4J_DATABASE=neo4j

TOP_K=5

[!TIP] Automatic Database Initialization: When you start the FastAPI server, app/database.py automatically enables the pgvector extension, creates the users, documents, and document_chunks tables and indexes in Neon PostgreSQL, and creates uniqueness constraints in Neo4j. You can also run sql/schema.sql manually in the Neon SQL Editor if desired.

docs.title: Step 4: Start the FastAPI Server
docs.text:
uvicorn app.api:app --reload

Verify the server is running: - API Root / Health: http://localhost:8000/health - Interactive Swagger Docs: http://localhost:8000/docs

docs.title: 3. Frontend Setup
docs.text:
Open a second terminal window:

cd /path/to/adk_rag/frontend
npm install
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:5173 in your browser to access the application.

docs.title: 4. Building & Serving the MkDocs Documentation
docs.text:
To view this documentation site in your browser with the Material theme and Mermaid diagrams:

source .venv/bin/activate
pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8001

Open http://127.0.0.1:8001 in your browser.

docs.title: Technical Specifications
docs.text: Complete engineering specifications for the ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform—covering runtime versions, database DDL and Cypher schemas, cryptographic authentication parameters, hybrid retrieval formulas, structured extraction models, and API contracts.

docs.title: 1. Technology Stack Matrix
docs.text: Layer Component Package / Technology Version / Model Purpose Backend Runtime Language Python 3.10+ (3.12 recommended) Core backend runtime API Server Web Framework FastAPI + Uvicorn fastapi >= 0.110, uvicorn[standard] Async REST API & OpenAPI documentation Agent Framework Orchestration Google Agent Development Kit (google-adk) Latest (LlmAgent, Runner, InMemorySessionService) Multi-tool agent reasoning & session management Reasoning LLM Agent Model Google Gemini (google-genai) gemini-2.5-pro (configurable via AGENT_MODEL) Tool selection, multi-hop synthesis, cited responses Graph Extraction LLM Structured Output Model Google Gemini (google-genai) gemini-2.5-flash (configurable via GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL) Fast JSON schema extraction of entities & relationships Embeddings Embedding Model Google Gemini (google-genai) gemini-embedding-001 (768 dimensions) Dense semantic vector representation of chunks & queries Relational + Vector DB Primary Database Neon Console Serverless PostgreSQL PostgreSQL 15/16 + pgvector (vector extension) User auth, document metadata, vector search, full-text search Postgres Driver DB Client psycopg2-binary + pgvector psycopg2-binary >= 2.9, pgvector >= 0.2.5 Threaded connection pooling & vector type registration Knowledge Graph DB Graph Database Neo4j AuraDB / Neo4j 5+ Neo4j 5.x (neo4j >= 5.18) Entity nodes, relationship triplets, multi-hop Cypher traversal Authentication Password + Token Python hashlib + hmac PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 + HS256 JWT Stateless Bearer authentication backed by Neon PostgreSQL Frontend UI Web Client React + Vite React 18.3, Vite 5.x, lucide-react Bioluminescent Neural Forest UI & interactive SVG Knowledge Graph

docs.title: 2. Database Schemas & Indexing
3. Authentication & Cryptographic Security (app/auth.py)
docs.text:
• Password Hashing (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256)

    • Work Factor: 260,000 iterations (OWASP standard)
    • Salt: 16 cryptographic random bytes (32 hex chars) per user via secrets.token_hex(16)
    • Verification: Constant-time digest comparison via hmac.compare_digest()

  • Stateless Bearer Token (HS256 JWT)

    • Algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 signed with JWT_SECRET_KEY
    • Default TTL: 168 hours (7 days, configurable via JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS)
    • Claims: sub (user_id), email, name, iat, exp

docs.title: 4.1 Structure-Aware Semantic Chunker (app/chunking.py)
docs.text:
• Chunk Size: 1,200 characters
  • Sliding Overlap: 200 characters
  • Splitting Priority: Markdown headings (#, ##, ###) → double-newline paragraphs (\n\n) → sentence boundaries ((?<=[.!?])\s+) → hard character slice fallback.

docs.title: 4.2 Batched Vector Embeddings (app/embeddings.py)
docs.text:
• Model: gemini-embedding-001
  • Output Dimensionality: 768 floats
  • Batch Size: Up to 50 chunks per API request

docs.title: 4.3 Hybrid Search Scoring Formula (app/rag_store.py)
docs.text:
For a user query \(q\) with embedding \(\mathbf{e}_q \in \mathbb{R}^{768}\) and a candidate chunk \(c\) with embedding \(\mathbf{e}_c \in \mathbb{R}^{768}\):

  1. Cosine Vector Similarity (pgvector <=> cosine distance operator): $\(\text{vector\_similarity}(c, q) = 1 - \left( \mathbf{e}_c \iff \mathbf{e}_q \right)\)$

  2. Full-Text Cover-Density Rank (PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd): $\(\text{keyword\_score}(c, q) = \text{ts\_rank\_cd}\left(\text{to\_tsvector}(\text{'english'}, c.\text{content}),\ \text{plainto\_tsquery}(\text{'english'}, q)\right)\)$

  3. Weighted Hybrid Score (70% semantic + 30% lexical): $\(\text{combined\_score}(c, q) = 0.7 \times \text{vector\_similarity}(c, q) + 0.3 \times \text{keyword\_score}(c, q)\)$

docs.title: 5. Gemini Structured Output Schema (app/graph_store.py)
docs.text:
During Step 5 of ingestion, chunks are grouped in batches of 4 (up to 25 chunks per document) and passed to gemini-2.5-flash with response_mime_type="application/json" and temperature=0.1:

app/graph_store.py
class ExtractedEntity(BaseModel):
    name: str          # Canonical entity name (e.g., "Google ADK", "PostgreSQL")
    category: str      # Person | Organization | Technology | Concept | Location | Event | Process | Metric | Model
    description: str   # Concise 1-sentence summary in context

class ExtractedRelationship(BaseModel):
    source: str        # Exact name of source entity
    target: str        # Exact name of target entity
    relation_type: str # UPPER_SNAKE_CASE verb (e.g., "USES", "DEPENDS_ON", "BUILT_BY")
    fact: str          # Concise factual sentence explaining how source relates to target

class ChunkGraphExtraction(BaseModel):
    entities: List[ExtractedEntity]
    relationships: List[ExtractedRelationship]

docs.title: 6. Environment Configuration Reference (.env)
docs.text: Variable Required Default Description GOOGLE_API_KEY Yes — Google Gemini API key from Google AI Studio DATABASE_URL Yes — Neon Console PostgreSQL connection URI (postgresql://...?sslmode=require) NEO4J_URI Yes bolt://localhost:7687 Neo4j AuraDB (neo4j+s://...) or local Bolt URI NEO4J_USERNAME Yes neo4j Neo4j username NEO4J_PASSWORD Yes — Neo4j password NEO4J_DATABASE No neo4j Target Neo4j database name JWT_SECRET_KEY No Auto-default Secret key for signing HS256 JWT tokens JWT_EXPIRE_HOURS No 168 JWT token validity period in hours AGENT_MODEL No gemini-2.5-pro Gemini model used by the Google ADK reasoning agent GRAPH_EXTRACTION_MODEL No gemini-2.5-flash Gemini model used for structured entity/relationship extraction TOP_K No 5 Default number of chunks returned by vector and hybrid search

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: Solutions for common issues encountered when running the ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform.

docs.title: ERROR: database "...sslmode=require" does not exist or connection is insecure (try using sslmode=require)
docs.text:
Cause: The DATABASE_URL in .env was missing the ? query separator before sslmode=require.

Fix: Ensure your DATABASE_URL in .env includes ?sslmode=require: 

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@ep-xxx.region.aws.neon.tech/dbname?sslmode=require
(Note: app/database.py also includes _normalize_database_url() to auto-repair missing ? delimiters at runtime.)

docs.title: Neo4j GqlStatusObject 01N51: warn: relationship type does not exist (RELATES_TO)
docs.text:
Cause: Neo4j 5+ emits informational GQL notifications when querying relationship types or node labels on a newly created, empty database before any document has been ingested.

Fix: 1. app/database.py suppresses these harmless notifications via NotificationMinimumSeverity.OFF. 2. Restart uvicorn app.api:app --reload or upload your first document to create the initial :Entity and :RELATES_TO elements.

docs.title: Neo4j connection warning on startup
docs.text:
Cause: NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USERNAME, NEO4J_PASSWORD, or NEO4J_DATABASE in .env does not match your running Neo4j instance, or your Neo4j AuraDB instance is paused.

Fix: - Check your credentials in .env. - If using Neo4j AuraDB Free tier, verify in the Aura Console that your instance is Running (Aura Free instances pause after inactivity) and that NEO4J_DATABASE matches your database name.

docs.title: [vite] http proxy error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8000
docs.text:
Cause: The Vite frontend dev server (http://localhost:5173) is trying to proxy API requests to http://127.0.0.1:8000, but the FastAPI backend is not running.

Fix: Start the FastAPI backend in a terminal from the project root: 

source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn app.api:app --reload

docs.title: [vite] http proxy error: /documents/upload (socket hang up / ECONNRESET)
docs.text:
Cause: Occurs if the FastAPI server restarts mid-upload or if the backend process is killed while processing a file.

Fix: app/api.py stores temporary upload files in the OS system temp directory (/tmp/adk_rag_uploads) outside the Uvicorn --reload watch tree and executes ingest_document in a background worker thread (asyncio.to_thread). Ensure you do not edit .py files in the project root while an upload is actively in progress.

docs.title: HTTP 401: Invalid or expired authentication token
docs.text:
Cause: Your JWT session token expired or JWT_SECRET_KEY was changed on the server.

Fix: Click Sign Out in the top-right header bar (or sign in again on the Sign In screen) to obtain a fresh JWT token.

docs.title: HTTP 400: Unsupported file type
docs.text:
Cause: The uploaded file extension is not in the supported list (for example, legacy .doc instead of .docx).

Fix: Convert the file to one of the supported extensions: .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .xls, .pptx, .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .xml, .html, .log.

docs.title: ValueError: No readable text was found in the document
docs.text:
Cause: The uploaded PDF contains scanned images without an embedded text layer, or the file is empty.

Fix: Run OCR on scanned PDFs before uploading, or verify the document contains selectable text.

docs.title: Interactive User Guide
docs.text: This step-by-step guide walks you through every screen and interaction in the ADK Agentic RAG + Knowledge Graph platform—from signing in with Neon PostgreSQL Authentication to monitoring the live 5-step ingestion pipeline, querying the Google ADK Agent, and exploring your interactive Neo4j Knowledge Graph.

docs.title: Step 1: Create an Account or Sign In
docs.text:
When you open the application (http://localhost:5173), the Bioluminescent Neural Forest Authentication Screen appears in front of the Tree of Knowledge backdrop.

Create a New Account Sign In to Existing Account
  1. Click the Create Account tab on the authentication card.
  2. Enter your credentials:
  3. Full Name: Your display name (e.g., Drona Sharma), shown in the top navigation bar.
  4. Email Address: Your email address (e.g., drona@company.com).
  5. Password: At least 6 characters (hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 using 260,000 iterations).
  6. Click Create Account & Continue →.
  7. Your user record is created in the Neon PostgreSQL users table and you are signed in immediately.
  1. Select the Sign In tab.
  2. Enter your registered Email Address and Password.
  3. Click Sign In to Workspace →.

Strict Multi-Tenant Isolation

Every document you upload, every vector chunk stored in Neon PostgreSQL, and every entity/relationship node created in Neo4j is strictly scoped to your authenticated user_id. No other user can view or query your workspace data.

docs.title: Step 2: Navigating the Workspace Header & 5-Tab Bar
docs.text:
Once authenticated, the workspace presents a sticky top header and a 5-tab workflow bar:

UI Element Location What It Shows API Online / Offline Pill Top-Right Header Real-time connectivity check against GET /health (API Online in glowing emerald when healthy). User Profile Badge Top-Right Header Displays your avatar initial, Full Name, and Email Address. Sign Out Button Top-Right Header Clears your JWT session token and returns you to the Sign In screen. 5-Tab Navigation Bar Below Header Ordered left-to-right following your natural workflow: Upload → Ingestion Pipeline → Documents → Agentic Chat → Knowledge Graph.

docs.title: Step 3: Uploading a Document
docs.text:
1. Select the Upload tab (active by default upon sign-in).
  2. Choose a Document:
  3. Drag and drop a file onto the bioluminescent dashed drop zone, or click anywhere inside the drop zone to browse your computer.
  4. Supported Formats: .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, .xls, .pptx, .txt, .md, .csv, .json, .xml, .html, .htm, .log.
  5. Verify the file preview card showing the filename and file size (click Remove if you want to pick a different file).
  6. Click Ingest into Neon Postgres & Neo4j.

Automatic Tab Switch

As soon as you click Ingest into Neon Postgres & Neo4j, the UI automatically switches you to the Ingestion Pipeline tab so you can watch the live 5-step execution in real time.

docs.title: Step 4: Monitoring the Live 5-Step Ingestion Pipeline
docs.text:
In the Ingestion Pipeline tab, only the currently active step spins/rotates, so you always know the exact operation executing on the backend:

  • Completed (Emerald Checkmark)

    The stage has finished executing for your document and displays its concrete output (e.g., characters extracted or chunks created).

  • Running Now… (Cyan Spinner)

    This is the exact stage currently executing on the FastAPI backend. The top live banner also shows the percentage progress bar.

  • Queued (Muted Badge)

    Upcoming stages waiting for the active step to finish.

docs.title: What Happens in Each Stage
docs.text:
1. Step 1 — Text Extraction (parsers.py): Extracts raw text using format-specific parsers (PyMuPDF, python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, etc.).
  2. Step 2 — Structure-Aware Semantic Chunking (chunking.py): Preserves headings and paragraphs while splitting text into 1,200-character chunks with a 200-character overlap.
  3. Step 3 — Gemini Embedding Generation (embeddings.py): Embeds chunks in batches using gemini-embedding-001 (768 dimensions).
  4. Step 4 — Neon PostgreSQL Vector & Hybrid Storage (rag_store.py): Bulk-inserts chunks, VECTOR(768) embeddings (HNSW index), and tsvector full-text index (GIN) into Neon PostgreSQL.
  5. Step 5 — Neo4j Knowledge Graph Extraction (graph_store.py): Uses gemini-2.5-flash Structured Outputs to extract domain entities and factual relationships and merges them into Neo4j.

Completion Summary Banner

When all 5 stages complete, an emerald banner titled All 5 Pipeline Steps Completed Successfully displays the Filename, Chunks (pgvector), Entities (Neo4j), Relationships (Neo4j), and Characters extracted.

docs.title: Step 5: Managing Your Documents (Documents Tab)
docs.text:
Switch to the Documents tab to view or delete files in your workspace:

  • Per-Document Badges: Each document card shows its chunks count (in Neon Postgres), entities count (in Neo4j), and relations count (in Neo4j).
  • Cascade Delete:
  • Click Delete on any document card.
  • Click Yes, delete on the confirmation prompt (Delete from Postgres & Neo4j?).
  • The backend atomically removes the document and its vector chunks from Neon PostgreSQL, deletes its RELATES_TO edges and Document node in Neo4j, and prunes any orphaned entity nodes.

docs.title: Step 6: Asking Questions in Agentic Chat (Agentic Chat Tab)
docs.text:
Switch to the Agentic Chat tab to query your documents using the Google ADK LlmAgent.

  1. Click a Suggested Question Chip on the starter screen, or type your question in the input box at the bottom.
  2. Press Enter to send (or Shift+Enter to insert a newline).

docs.title: Understanding Tool Badges & Dual Citations
docs.text:
The ADK agent autonomously selects one or more of its 4 specialized tools and displays Tool Execution Badges at the top of its reply:

Tool Badge Database Queried When the Agent Chooses It hybrid_search Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector + FTS) Default for most questions; combines 70% semantic similarity + 30% keyword matching. vector_search Neon PostgreSQL (pgvector) Broad conceptual or thematic questions. graph_search Neo4j Knowledge Graph Questions about entities, technologies, people, or how concepts connect. get_entity_relationships Neo4j Knowledge Graph Deep-dive traversal into a specific entity's 1-hop neighborhood.

Every assistant response includes inline verifiable citations: - Document Chunk Citation: [Source: filename.pdf, chunk 3] (highlighted in emerald) - Knowledge Graph Citation: [Graph: Google ADK -> USES -> Gemini 2.5 Pro] (highlighted in gold)

docs.title: Step 7: Exploring the Neo4j Knowledge Graph (Knowledge Graph Tab)
docs.text:
Switch to the Knowledge Graph tab to visually explore the entities and relationships extracted from your documents:

  1. Filter by Category Pills: Click All, Technology, Model, Concept, Organization, Person, Metric, Location, or Event to isolate specific node types.
  2. Real-Time Search: Type any keyword into the filter bar to highlight matching entities, relationship types, or facts.
  3. Interactive SVG Topology:
  4. Click any node on the glowing neural canvas to highlight its 1-hop neighborhood and inspect its description and relationships in the right-hand Entity Inspector panel.
  5. Click any entity name in the Extracted Relationship Facts list on the right to center and select that node on the graph.
  6. Click Clear on the selected entity card to return to the full graph view.
